But she was only ready at around 5.45am. Because of this delay the couple lost almost one hour of their photoshoot. This is very unprofessional and don’t know what she did for more than 6 hours just to dress the bride. Another disappointing issue was with the bride’s mother’s dressing. The salon had already agreed to do it but just two days before the wedding, they told us they would only do it if we paid an extra Rs. 9,000. We felt this was very unfair and unprofessional. After all the waiting and stress we expected the bridal makeup to be beautiful. Sadly, it wasn’t. The eye makeup was not blended well (whole eye was black) and was extended too far, which did not look nice. Also it was shocking to see the foundation and makeup melting during the photoshoot. We were really disappointed. The most shocking part was when the makeup artist used a sponge on the flower girl that had visible fungus on it (I have attached a picture of the sponge). This is a serious hygiene issue and should never happen. After taking Rs 12,000 for a small flower girl if the salon cannot provide a clean or a new sponge for a client they should at least ask clients to bring their own. After charging so much for bridal services providing a clean sponge should not be a problem. At the end of the day, the bride and our whole family were very disappointed with the service. A wedding day is already stressful and a bridal salon should make the experience easier not more stressful. Sadly, we felt that the team cared more about making money than keeping their promises maintaining proper hygiene and giving good customer service. Based on our experience, I would not recommend Salon Chamya & Academy to anyone looking for bridal dressing services.

I recently visited this salon after moving houses and chose it based on Google reviews. Unfortunately, my experience was far from satisfactory. Here's a breakdown:

Haircut Quality:

After the hair cut, my friends did not recognise anything new.

Hygiene Standards:

1. The chair was covered with cut hair from previous clients, including the armrests.

Space and Comfort:

Customer Service:

3 I declined the wash and massage after seeing the lack of hygiene, but what surprised me was the lack of basic styling after the cut. No wax, no offer to style my hair, and no effort to check if I was satisfied with the result.

For context, I've been visiting salons for 25+ years, including high-end places like Chagall, as well as mid-range options. I’ve never encountered this level of poor hygiene and service.

Poor Appointment Management at Dee’s I have been a loyal customer of Dee’s Piliyandala for quite some time, mainly because my long-time hairdresser, Lushan, who has taken care of my hair since childhood, works here. Over the years, I’ve also received various other services at this branch and have never had any major complaints — until my most recent visit on 7th December. I had made an appointment two months in advance with Kavindi at 4:00 PM for a special dressing for my best friend’s wedding. Given the importance of the event, I even called the day before to reconfirm the appointment. Unfortunately, what followed was extremely disappointing and stressful. I arrived early at 3:45 PM to get my eyebrows threaded before the makeup. The branch manager, Sampath, directed me to the makeup room and said he would send someone for the eyebrows. I waited patiently, but no one came. At 4:23 PM, after waiting far too long, I had to remind him again — only then did he send someone to do the eyebrows. During this time, Kavindi was still occupied with another dressing, despite my prior booking. I ended up waiting past 5:00 PM, growing increasingly anxious as I was supposed to be getting ready for a wedding, not sitting unattended in a salon. Thankfully, one staff member, Chamila, noticed that I had been left waiting. When I explained the situation, she immediately stepped in and took responsibility for dressing me. She was quick, kind, and efficient — and I truly appreciate her help. However, by the time the dressing was finished, I was already running late for the wedding, and I had to rush out. To make matters worse, Sampath was nowhere to be found, leaving me without any explanation or apology for the delay and mismanagement. Is this really the level of customer service Dee’s aims to provide? I completely understand that December is a busy festive season for salons, but appointments for events — especially those booked months in advance — must be handled with professionalism and respect. Delays like this have real consequences for customers. I am sharing this experience not out of anger, but because I believe no one else should have to go through the same uncomfortable and stressful situation. I would really appreciate a proper explanation and hope the management takes steps to improve their appointment handling and customer care in the future.

When I pointed it out to him and told him that the hair was not cut properly, his reply was that it could not be. "And I want my hair to be shorter," I told him. "Oyata patta ketha wei ah," he said again. "I don't mind if I am ugly or not. Convenience is important to me." I told him. When I told him to look more closely, he again moved the trimmer just once behind my hair. I was very disappointed. After that, the guy who colored my hair came there and asked Supun, "May I set her hair?", but I saw in the mirror that Supun nodded and said that doesn't want to do it. I am not someone who went to a salon to get a haircut for the first time in my life. As someone who does different hair styles all the time, I can understand how unprofessional they were. Also, I don't get service from them for free. And apart from providing the service I needed, I didn't need their comments just as "patta ketha wei". Therefore, I do not recommend this kind of salon to anyone who does not know their service and limitations.

I’m reposting this review because it’s come to my attention that the salon is now engaging in damage control: soliciting 5-star reviews and possibly posting fake ones to cover up genuine customer feedback. I believe future clients deserve transparency. I just washed and styled my hair for the first time since yesterday’s so-called “curly trim,” and it’s even worse than I initially thought. The cut is choppy, uneven, and has absolutely no layering. My hair now looks like a child’s haircut, completely undoing years of growth and care. Curly hair requires time and attention, especially for trims. Instead, I was kept waiting for 30+ minutes, only to receive a “trim” that took less than 3 minutes and involved aggressively yanking through dry curls and chopping chunks off without proper sectioning or method. This review is not intended to harm small businesses but to protect fellow curly-haired clients who trust salons to treat their hair with the care it deserves. I urge the salon to reflect and improve rather than silence or bury negative feedback. 1. Appointment Expectations: When I made the appointment, I specifically asked for a curly trim and was told it would take 30 minutes. I was also advised that I did not need to wash my hair before coming. 2. Timing and Delay: I arrived on time at 9am. Despite that, I was kept waiting for around 30 minutes without explanation. This was frustrating, especially as I had a follow-up appointment at 10am, which I had to reschedule due to the delay. 3. CAD Cut Wasn’t Feasible: Since I had already been delayed, it wouldn’t have been possible to opt for a longer CAD cut even if I had wanted one, so blaming the experience on me declining it isn’t fair. 4. Trim Quality: I’ve had curly trims before, both from specialists and regular stylists. A proper trim involves assessing the curls individually to maintain their shape and health. At your salon, my back hair was cut in one go, followed by the sides. The entire “trim” took under 3 minutes, with no attention to my curl pattern or layering. After making me wait 30–40 minutes, it felt rushed and careless. Had I known this was what a trim meant at your salon, I would have either gone to a standard hairdresser or done it myself. 5. Detangling Method: The way my dry hair was combed was extremely rough and painful, causing visible breakage. No other stylist I’ve seen has handled my curls so aggressively. 6. Emotional Impact: I had spent two years growing my hair out, and in one short appointment, that progress was erased. I was genuinely upset when I saw the result; it was not the length or shape I had asked for. 7. Defensive Response: I’m reposting my review because instead of acknowledging the impact of what happened and showing a willingness to learn, the salon chose to defend the experience and shift the blame onto me. 8. About CAD Cuts: Your CAD cut may be effective for some, but please be aware it is not a new or unique technique. It’s a variation of the Curly Girl Method, a well-known global approach to curly hair. The issue isn’t with your CAD cut service, but with how trims are handled. 9. Inconsistent Communication: If the appointment was supposed to take 30 minutes, why did the haircut itself take barely two? I hope this feedback is taken in the spirit it’s intended: to help you improve your service to curly-haired clients, especially those coming in for trims and not full styling sessions.

I am writing this review to express my disappointment with the unprofessional service I received yesterday at Salon PR.

I arrived about five minutes before my scheduled appointment; however, I had to wait over 30 minutes before my pedicure even began. During the pedicure, the staff member attending to me was called away by the receptionist, which further delayed the process. The pack needs to be kept for 15 minutes, however, it was on for more than 30 min due to this. Although my second scheduled service was arranged shortly afterward, I still experienced an additional waiting time of approximately 15 minutes. I would like to note that the staff members who provided the services were pleasant, friendly, and professional, and I was satisfied with the quality of their work.

My dissatisfaction lies with the front desk management. The appointments were not handled efficiently, leading to unnecessary and excessive delays. If adequate staff or service capacity was not available on that day, an excessive number of appointments should not have been accepted. While a delay of 10-15 minutes is understandable, longer delays significantly affect customer comfort and disrupt personal schedules. After all, appointments are made with the expectation that services will be provided within a reasonable timeframe.

I chose Salon PR because of the professionalism I experienced in the past; however, appointment mismanagement of this nature can negatively affect the overall quality and reputation of the salon. On a previous visit, I had the opportunity to meet Mr. Pathum Rukshan, who personally inquired about my experience, which was very positive at the time. I am confident that Mr. Pathum values his customers and the standards of the salon, and I trust that he will take the necessary steps to ensure such issues do not recur.

I visited this salon about three weeks ago and repeatedly explained that I wanted an even dark brown color throughout my hair. I specifically told the stylist that I did not want highlights or a lighter shade. The stylist advised that my hair needed mild bleaching first because I had been covering my grey roots for over two years. She showed me that my previous color had built up on my hair and assured me that bleaching was necessary to achieve the dark brown shade I wanted. Trusting her professional advice, I agreed. Immediately after the service, the color looked acceptable under the salon lighting, although it was lighter than I had requested. However, after I returned home and saw it in natural light, I noticed that it was much lighter than I had asked for. My hair also had a mixture of dark brown, golden, and reddish tones, and some sections had not taken the color at all and remained close to their original color. More importantly, the color was uneven. Some sections were noticeably lighter than others, making it look as though I had highlights, even though I had specifically requested that I did not want highlights. While the color itself is not unattractive and suits my skin tone, it is not the result I clearly requested. I also noticed that the lighter sections of my hair became dry and frizzy after the bleaching process, leaving my hair in a much drier condition than before. Throughout the consultation, I repeatedly expressed that I did not want a lighter shade. The stylist kept telling me to trust her because she would create a “beautiful” color. However, beauty is subjective. As a customer, I expected the salon to achieve the color I specifically requested rather than choosing what they believed would look best. Unfortunately, my experience did not meet my expectations, and I cannot recommend this salon for hair coloring services.
